pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: APOLOGY LETTER

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why do we write apology letters?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify key elements of an apology letter for comprehension
2. write an apology letter seeking reconciliation for effective communication

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter makes your writing clear so others can read it easily.

• Look at the model your teacher shows. Notice shape, order, and spacing.

• Practise slowly first, then build neat speed.

• Check your work: Did you spell carefully? Did you use correct marks?

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Copy three model sentences neatly, leaving finger spaces between words.

Example 2: Spell five lesson words aloud, then write them without looking.

Example 3: Fix this sentence by adding capital letters and a full stop: “amina went to kisumu”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Write five neat sentences about your school using words from this topic.
2. Exchange books with a friend and check spelling or punctuation together.
3. Rewrite one messy sentence so it is clear and correct.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Complete a short guided paragraph in your exercise book.
2. List eight words from this topic and practise spelling them with a parent.
3. Write a short note to a friend using correct punctuation.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss the format of writing a letter,
2. Critical thinking and problem solving: This is enhanced as the learner explores views when identifying words and phrases used to express remorse or apologies.
3. Communication and Collaboration: This is acquired as the learner engages actively when discussing samples of apology letters accessed from digital devices, with peers. 54 Values:
4. Respect: This is enhanced as the learner accommodates and gives input when sharing their work for peer review and suggestions for improvement.
5. Ensure every learner actively participates in the activity

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we write apology letters?
2. what went well and why ● what did not go well and why?
3. what can be done differently next time?
4. what have they learnt?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Neat writing helps the reader.
2. Check spelling and punctuation before you finish.
3. Practice a little every day.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
